questions.prompt: The person approves a danger-full-access escalation for `npm install`. The model then runs `rm -rf dist` with no escalation fields. Under which mode does it run?
options: danger-full-access, because the session was widened
read-only, as a penalty for escalating
The person is asked again automatically
workspace-write, because the wider mode applied to that one call only
questions.explanation: The approved mode is returned for one call and stored nowhere. Every later call runs under the session's normal mode.

questions.prompt: The current mode is workspace-write and the model asks for sandbox_permissions: "workspace-write" with a reason. What happens?
options: The call runs under workspace-write with no prompt, because nothing wider was asked for
The person is asked to approve it
It is refused as not strictly wider
questions.explanation: Asking for the mode you already have gives nothing away, so it returns the current mode without an approval prompt.

questions.prompt: Why does a rejected escalation tell the model to "stop and explain instead of working around it"?
options: So the model retries with a longer justification
Because the model might otherwise reach the same goal another way, such as through a file tool, defeating the person's no
Because rejected calls crash the agent loop
So the sandbox runner is probed again
questions.explanation: A no should mean no. Telling the model to stop and explain keeps it from finding another route to the same refused effect.
